content:
miguel: Heads-up — multiple customers hitting 502/504s from hosted API front-door starting ~2024-06-16T09:12:36Z. Spike lasted ~15m. Primary symptom: edge returns 502 with upstream reset or 504 on long streams. Example req id: req_0a1b2c.

tara: Seeing same in support dashboard. Customers complaining timeout + degraded streaming. Ticket ids: INC-3492, INC-3493.

miguel: Repro steps from support: simple curl to /v1/generate with API key from prod, small payload. Intermittent 502s. Minimal curl: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` — some requests fail with `upstream prematurely closed connection` in envoy logs.

sophie: Pulling envoy logs for the window. Early signal: a bunch of `stream reset: code 2` and `recv timeout` from the upstream pool. Also saw `upstream connection reuses: 0` spikes.

jamal: Any recent deploys? deploy-bot: can you paste the last deploy hashes for prod and edge?

deploy-bot: Prod gateway deploy: git@redwood:gateway@sha:7e3f2a4 (deployed 2024-06-16T08:58:12Z). Edge sidecar: git@redwood:edge-proxy@sha:9b1c4d0 (deployed 2024-06-15). No config rollouts in the last 24h.

sophie: Correlating with infra metrics — we see a surge in auth backend latency (token-validate calls) at the same time. 99th auth latency jumped from 30ms -> 1.2s. Upstream auth errors returned 429s for a subset of calls.

miguel: That matches one customer repro: their calls include a live billing header that triggers an auth lookup per request. If auth backend is throttling, edge may drop upstream connections -> 502.

tara: Is there any sign of h2 window exhaustion? streaming endpoints show a few long-lived streams; maybe KV cache misses + auth lookup per stream header causes head-of-line blocking.

sophie: I pulled a sample envoy trace for req_0a1b2c: timeline shows: accept -> auth backend call (600ms) -> upstream connect -> upstream reset. Envoy logs show `upstream reset before response` shortly after auth backend returned 429 for other flows.

jamal: Quick mitigation options: 1) Enable auth caching at gateway for token validations (short TTL) 2) Bypass auth call for known internal routes temporarily 3) Increase auth backend rate cap for prod for next 30m

miguel: Support ask: can we enable a protective fallback so customer traffic doesn't see 502s? Prefer non-code change if possible.

sophie: I can flip auth-cache=on in the gateway config for prod (short TTL 10s) via a config flag — low risk. Will also bump upstream connection pool size by +20%.

deploy-bot: Rolling config change: gateway.auth_cache.enabled=true, gateway.auth_cache.ttl=10s — started at 2024-06-16T09:25:10Z.

observability-bot: Alert suppression: suppr(alerts:gateway-502-spike) for 30m applied by sophie.

tara: After auth-cache flip, 502 rate dropped ~85% within 2 minutes. Customers report recovery. Still seeing a small tail of 504 on long streams.

sophie: For the 504 tail, I increased upstream idle and stream timeouts by 10s to accommodate long embeddings streams. Also tuned h2 window sizes on the proxy.

jamal: Any customer-side mitigations we should recommend?

miguel: Ask customers to: 1) Retry on 502 with small backoff 2) Use connection pooling clients to avoid per-request auth churn 3) If high-rate, use token caching at app layer

tara: I updated both tickets with mitigation steps and customer-facing notes. Marking as escalated -> mitigated.

miguel: Action items: 
- infra: sophie to run postmortem on auth backend ratecap + consider auto-cache fallback (owner: sophie)
- infra: jamal to evaluate permanent increase of upstream pool sizes and h2 tuning (owner: jamal)
- support: tara to confirm customer impact and close tickets (owner: tara)

sophie: Will collect logs/traces and open a postmortem doc. Preliminary root cause: auth validation rate limit causing cascade to edge upstream resets under bursty small-request workloads.

miguel: Thanks team. Customer comms drafted, sending now. Please paste any additional traces here. :thumbsup:

tara: Closing the loop: customers acknowledged, one customer requested SLA credit; routed to finance.

jamal: I'll follow up with a load test to validate cache-on config at scale.

sophie: Postmortem doc link (draft): https://docs.redwood.ai/postmortems/pm-auth-cache-2024-06-16 — will fill details and timelines.

miguel: Good work. Will convert to a formal incident report if we find a config/design gap. :eyes:
